source_meta._title: All arrow types lose their name/NBT data when shot and picked up

stor.environment: Minecraft Java Edition 1.4.2 in a new single-player world using the integrated server. Begin in Creative mode with cheats enabled so the bow, arrows, and anvil can be obtained deterministically and the arrows can be renamed without acquiring experience levels. Change to Survival mode before firing so the bow uses an arrow from the custom-named stack. Use default controls unless the corresponding actions have been rebound.
preconditions: Launch exactly Minecraft Java Edition 1.4.2, the first version listed as affected; do not use fix version 23w43a.
Create a new single-player world with Game Mode set to Creative and Allow Cheats enabled.
Use an unmodified client without gameplay-changing mods or datapacks.
Keep at least one empty inventory slot available for the recovered arrow.
Use a plain, unenchanted bow; in particular, do not use an Infinity-enchanted bow.
Prepare a clear patch of solid ground where an arrow can be fired into a block a few blocks away and recovered without falling into water, fire, lava, a void, or an inaccessible gap.
Do not carry any ordinary, unnamed arrows other than the stack that will be renamed; this prevents an unnamed recovered arrow from merging into an unrelated stack.

steps.action: From the title screen, select Singleplayer, choose Create New World, set Game Mode to Creative, enable Allow Cheats under the additional world options, and create the world. Wait until terrain has rendered and movement responds normally.
steps.success_cue: The player is standing in a loaded single-player world, can fly, has no health or hunger bars, and can use commands.

steps.action: Locate a clear area with solid ground. If necessary, fly a short distance from trees, water, lava, cliffs, or other obstacles, then land.
steps.success_cue: There is a visible solid ground surface at least several blocks long, with enough room to shoot and walk to an embedded arrow.

steps.action: Press the inventory action key, default E, to open the Creative inventory.
steps.success_cue: The Creative inventory interface is open and item categories or the item search interface are visible.

steps.action: Find the Bow item in the Creative inventory and place one plain bow into an empty hotbar slot. The hotbar is the row of nine slots at the bottom of the inventory.
steps.success_cue: A plain bow is visible in one of the nine hotbar slots.

steps.action: Find the Arrow item and place one stack of regular arrows into a separate inventory or hotbar slot. Do not obtain any additional unnamed arrow stacks.
steps.success_cue: One stack of regular arrows is present and no other arrow stacks are in the inventory.

steps.action: Find the Anvil item and place one anvil into another hotbar slot.
steps.success_cue: An anvil item is visible in the hotbar.

steps.action: Close the inventory with E. Select the hotbar slot containing the anvil by pressing its corresponding number key, aim at the top of a solid ground block, and right-click to place it. Minecraft 1.4.2 added anvils and supports renaming items with them. ([ru.minecraft.wiki](https://ru.minecraft.wiki/w/1.4.2_%28Java_Edition%29?utm_source=openai))
steps.success_cue: A placed anvil block is visible directly in front of the player.

steps.action: Aim at the placed anvil and right-click it to open the anvil interface.
steps.success_cue: The anvil interface is open, showing a left input slot, a right input slot, a name field, and an output slot.

steps.action: Move the entire regular-arrow stack into the anvil's left input slot. Click the name field, remove the existing item name if one is displayed, and type the custom name exactly as supplied by the report.
steps.success_cue: The name field contains exactly MC-1981 and a renamed arrow stack is available in the output slot.

steps.action: Click the output slot to take the renamed arrow stack and place it in an inventory or hotbar slot. Leave the right anvil input slot empty. In Creative mode, the anvil operation is not blocked by the normal experience-level limit. ([ru.minecraft.wiki](https://ru.minecraft.wiki/w/1.4.2_%28Java_Edition%29?utm_source=openai))
steps.success_cue: Hovering over the arrow stack in the inventory displays the custom item name MC-1981.

steps.action: Close the anvil interface with E. Ensure that the plain bow and the MC-1981 arrow stack remain in the inventory and that at least one other inventory slot is empty.
steps.success_cue: Normal world view is visible; the bow and custom-named arrows remain available, and an empty inventory slot exists.

steps.action: Press T to open in-game chat, enter the historical game-mode command exactly with the leading slash, and press Enter. Numeric game-mode arguments and mode-first command ordering were supported by the command implementation used in this period. ([minecraft.wiki](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Minecraft_Wiki%3AIssues/Weekly_12w37a?utm_source=openai))
steps.success_cue: Chat reports a successful game-mode change, and the Survival health, hunger, and armor interface appears above the hotbar.

steps.action: Press E and re-check the arrow stack before shooting. Hover over it and confirm that it is still named MC-1981, then close the inventory.
steps.success_cue: The pre-shot arrow stack still displays MC-1981, and the game has returned to normal first-person view in Survival mode.

steps.action: Select the hotbar slot containing the plain bow by pressing the corresponding number key or scrolling the mouse wheel. Confirm that the renamed arrow stack remains elsewhere in the inventory as ammunition.
steps.success_cue: The bow is visible in the player's hand, and the MC-1981 arrow stack is present in the inventory.

steps.action: Stand approximately 3 to 6 blocks from a clear patch of solid ground. Aim downward at a ground block far enough ahead that the fired arrow can visibly embed in the block instead of striking the player or traveling out of sight.
steps.success_cue: The crosshair points at an unobstructed solid ground block a few blocks in front of the player.

steps.action: Hold right-click, the default Use Item control, until the bow is fully drawn.
steps.success_cue: The bow model is visibly pulled back to its fully drawn state while the crosshair remains aimed at the target ground block.

steps.action: Release right-click once to fire exactly one arrow into the targeted ground block. Do not fire additional arrows.
steps.success_cue: One arrow is visibly embedded in the ground, and the custom-named arrow stack's count has decreased by one.

steps.action: Wait until the fired arrow is stationary and remains embedded in the ground. Do not open the inventory or inspect item data yet.
steps.success_cue: The arrow has stopped moving and is reachable by walking over it.

steps.action: Walk directly over the embedded arrow using the movement controls, normally W, until it is collected. Stop moving immediately after the arrow disappears from the ground.
steps.success_cue: The arrow entity disappears from the ground and the pickup sound plays or an arrow item is added to the inventory; the recovered item's name has not yet been evaluated.

stor.handoff_condition: The player has just walked over and collected the single arrow that was fired from the MC-1981 custom-named arrow stack. Stop further input and hand control to the observation subsystem for inventory and item-data inspection.
uncertainties: The report supplies `/give @s minecraft:arrow{display:{Name:'{"text":"MC-1981"}'}}`, but that exact command is not executable in the recommended Minecraft 1.4.2 environment. Custom item NBT support for `/give` was added in the 1.7.2 development cycle, after 1.4.2. The plan therefore preserves the required custom name by using the 1.4.2 anvil-renaming mechanic rather than silently rewriting the command into unsupported historical syntax. ([zh.minecraft.wiki](https://zh.minecraft.wiki/w/Java%E7%89%881.7.2?utm_source=openai))

The report does not prescribe a game mode, world type, seed, coordinates, or server type. A single-player Creative setup followed by Survival-mode firing is a practical deterministic choice, not a stated requirement of the report.

The issue title refers to all arrow types, but the supplied reproduction procedure specifically creates and fires a regular arrow. Minecraft 1.4.2 predates later tipped and spectral arrow variants, so this plan reproduces the report's regular-arrow case only.

The exact layout of the 1.4.2 Creative inventory depends on the selected item category. The executor may obtain Bow, Arrow, and Anvil through the available category tabs if a search field is not exposed in the current tab.
